approach: A stateless provider evaluates the engine-composed frozen initial input. It checks the authored artifact against its frozen schema, then applies the frozen review policy to the external evidence supplied for the exact checked transition. Nothing is stored between requests; every request is decided from the frozen input and the request alone.

elements.name: protocol boundary
elements.responsibility: Parse one strict request and emit one strict result per process, exactly as the existing Loop Engine provider boundary requires (intent constraint 3).

elements.name: structural checker
elements.responsibility: Check an authored artifact against its frozen schema and return every violated structural rule.

elements.name: evidence evaluator
elements.responsibility: Decide each configured axis from supplied external evidence: current subject revision only, and the configured number of distinct non-subject authors.

elements.name: terminal gate
elements.responsibility: Permit the reference workflow's terminal transition only after the configured validation obligations are satisfied.

decisions.choice: Speak the existing provider boundary unchanged: one strict request in, one strict result out, one request per process.
decisions.rationale: Intent constraint 3 requires compatibility with the existing Loop Engine provider boundary, which invokes one local subprocess per request.
rejected: Defining a new request or result shape: breaks intent constraint 3, which requires compatibility with the existing provider boundary.

decisions.choice: Report every violated structural rule in one deterministic pass.
decisions.rationale: A caller fixing a malformed artifact needs the whole list at once, and the denial is part of AC-2.
rejected: Reporting only the first violation: fails AC-2, which requires each violated structural rule to be named.

decisions.choice: Identify an author by the exact name and kind pair and exclude the subject author.
decisions.rationale: Distinctness and independence must be decidable from the supplied claims alone.
rejected: Identifying an author by name alone: fails AC-3, because a human and an agent sharing a name would count as one author and a duplicate could not be told apart.
Counting every submitted record as an author: fails AC-3, because duplicate records from one author would satisfy the author floor.

decisions.choice: Count only evidence recorded for the current subject revision.
decisions.rationale: Evidence about an earlier revision says nothing about the artifact now under review.
rejected: Counting evidence for any revision of the subject: fails AC-3, because stale evidence for an earlier revision would satisfy the obligation.

Binding evidence to hashes of the artifact bytes: not needed for AC-3, because the intent accepts an immaterial edit without a revision bump and requires a bump for every material edit, and cryptographic provenance is a stated non-goal.

decisions.choice: Decide every request from the frozen input alone, with no stored state.
decisions.rationale: The existing provider boundary starts one local subprocess per request and the frozen policies and schemas cannot change during a run.
rejected: Keeping a provider-side record of earlier evaluations: breaks the constraint of one local subprocess per request and lets a decision depend on state the caller cannot inspect.

risks.risk: An author may edit an artifact materially without changing its declared revision.
risks.mitigation: The external actor must bump the revision and obtain renewed review for material edits; recheck the current declared artifact at every approval boundary. The provider still trusts declared revisions and cannot detect dishonest same-revision edits. Only the intent's immaterial-edit residual is accepted; no hashing, locking, or provider-side semantic enforcement is added.

risks.risk: Exact name-kind declared identity is unauthenticated; a subject can claim another identity.
risks.mitigation: Provider preserves deterministic declared-identity checks; external process and provenance controls remain outside scope, so this residual is accepted.

coverage.acceptance: A caller can inspect the frozen policies and artifact schemas before evaluating a transition.
coverage.delivered_by: The engine freezes the initial input, including its policies and schemas, at start and show returns it before any transition is evaluated.

coverage.acceptance: A malformed subject artifact is denied with each violated structural rule named.
coverage.delivered_by: The structural checker returns every violated rule and the checked transition names each in its denial.

coverage.acceptance: A checked transition refuses stale, self-authored, duplicate-author, or configured-obligation-incomplete evidence.
coverage.delivered_by: The evidence evaluator counts only current-revision evidence from distinct non-subject authors and refuses any axis with too few distinct current-revision authors.

coverage.acceptance: The reference workflow reaches its terminal state only after its configured validation obligations are satisfied.
coverage.delivered_by: The terminal gate allows the terminal transition only after the configured validation obligations are satisfied.
